title: AfD Poised for First Post-War State Power in Germany as US Envoys Head to Kyiv After Three-Hour Putin Talks
subhead: Germany votes in a landmark Saxony-Anhalt election that could put the far right in state government for the first time since 1945, while Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner take the first trip of Trump's top negotiators to Kyiv after a three-hour meeting with Putin in Moscow.

sections.heading: Germany Votes: AfD Aims for First Post-War State Majority
sections.body:
Voters in Saxony-Anhalt went to the polls on Sunday in what the BBC calls a 'seismic' election for Germany's east. The far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), led by the 35-year-old Ulrich Siegmund, is polling ahead and could secure an outright majority in the regional parliament ' the first time a far-right party has held state-level power in Germany since World War Two, according to the BBC.

The vote is also a referendum on Chancellor Friedrich Merz. The embattled CDU leader, booed at recent public appearances, pledged to halt the rise of the far right and has instead seen it climb. The AfD campaign has promised migrant detention and deportation task-forces, segregated schooling for refugee children, and restrictions on LGBT symbols in schools, while courting voters frustrated by immigration, energy costs and German aid to Ukraine.
sections.whyItMatters: An AfD state majority would shatter a post-war German taboo, shift the centre of gravity of German politics eastward and put unprecedented pressure on a weakened CDU chancellor during an acute security crisis with Russia.

sections.heading: Ukraine Peace Track Reaches Kyiv
sections.body:
US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to land in Kyiv on Sunday, the first visit of President Donald Trump's top negotiators to the Ukrainian capital, after holding three hours of closed-door talks with Vladimir Putin at his Moscow residence on Saturday, the BBC reports. The White House said they discussed 'substantive plans for next steps' and an announcement is expected in the coming weeks.

In a notable confidence-building step, Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky agreed to halt strikes on each other's capitals for three days, and Zelensky said he was ready for 'a substantive conversation.' Putin adviser Yuri Ushakov described the Moscow talks as 'constructive, extremely frank,' saying economic issues and potential Russian-American projects were discussed at length, alongside the 'root causes of the conflict.' The diplomacy proceeds against a backdrop of intensified aerial attacks, with Ukraine short of interceptor missiles and refocusing strikes on Russian oil infrastructure.
sections.whyItMatters: US negotiators reaching Kyiv marks a concrete step from ceasefire talk into direct shuttle diplomacy, even as the strike pause on capitals suggests both sides are testing the ground for a real settlement.

sections.heading: US and Iran Trade Tanker Strikes as Naval War Sharpens
sections.body:
The US and Iran exchanged retaliatory attacks on ships on Saturday in the sharpest flare-up since fighting resumed about a week ago. US Central Command said it had 'permanently disabled' two Iran-linked oil tankers, including one near Kharg Island the hub for about 90 percent of Iran's crude exports and 'completely destroyed' a third in the Gulf of Oman, according to Reuters and the BBC. Admiral Brad Cooper said Washington was imposing 'an even higher economic cost' after the IRGC fired ballistic missiles at a US aircraft carrier and guided-missile destroyer, which Centcom said evaded the attacks without casualties.

Iran's state media said the IRGC retaliated against six ships: three oil tankers transiting the Strait of Hormuz on what Tehran called unauthorised routes and three vessels it described as US-affiliated. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth wrote on social media: 'If Iran shoots at US ships, we will destroy (and sink) their oil tankers.' The exchange came a day after Trump dismissed the six-month conflict as 'small potatoes,' and as he separately threatened to strike Iran's fortified Pickaxe Mountain nuclear site near Natanz 'very soon,' a target he first floated in mid-July.
sections.whyItMatters: The campaign has shifted onto Iran's oil tanker fleet, attacking the revenue lines that fund the IRGC and its proxies, while Trump's nuclear-site threat keeps the prospect of a strike on Iran's remaining atomic infrastructure on the table.

sections.heading: US Sanctions Turkish Bank, Opening a New Alliance Friction Point
sections.body:
The US Treasury imposed sanctions on Golden Global Bank and its subsidiaries on Friday, accusing the Turkish lender of facilitating 'tens of millions of dollars' worth of transactions' for the IRGC-Qods Force and helping Iran's shadow banking system move oil revenue from China to Turkey using gold and cash, Al Jazeera reports. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent framed the action as part of 'Operation Economic Outcast,' Washington's drive to economically isolate Tehran.

The bank denied the claims, saying it had met all local and international compliance rules, and threatened legal action against the sanctions. The move injects new strain into US-Turkey ties at a sensitive moment, given Ankara's strategic position on NATO's flank and its independent line on the Iran war and the Israel-Syria file.
sections.whyItMatters: Targeting a Turkish bank pulls a NATO ally directly into Washington's economic war on Iran and tests the limits of the alliance relationship under dual pressure from US sanctions enforcement and Turkey's own foreign-policy independence.

sections.heading: Yemen's Front Reopens: Houthis Push Toward Bab al-Mandeb
sections.body:
The Yemen conflict flared into some of its worst fighting in years over the past week. A Houthi missile strike on a crowded road near Taiz killed at least four civilians, Al Jazeera reports, as a major Houthi offensive toward the Bab al-Mandeb strait triggered fierce clashes across Taiz and Hodeidah and rapid civilian displacement. In response, the internationally recognised Yemeni government launched its own air attacks on Houthi positions, a notable escalation in its military posture.

The fighting coincides with a broader regional squeeze on the strait, which alongside Hormuz controls one of the world's key energy chokepoints. Qatar, meanwhile, was removed from Fitch's negative watch list with the ratings agency citing eased risks to its LNG sites, a small sign that at least some Gulf energy infrastructure risk is being reassessed.
sections.whyItMatters: A renewed Houthi push on Bab al-Mandeb threatens to tighten the squeeze on Red Sea shipping and energy routes already disrupted by the Iran war, adding a second front to the regional chokepoint crisis.

bottomLine: The most consequential developments today were in Europe and the wider Iran war. Germany faces a landmark election that could put the far right in state government for the first time in its post-war history, a direct challenge to a weakened CDU chancellor in the middle of a security crisis. The Ukraine peace track moved from rhetoric to shuttle diplomacy as Trump's negotiators headed to Kyiv after three hours with Putin. And the US-Iran conflict sharpened into a tanker war, with Washington hitting Iran's oil fleet, Tehran retaliating against ships in Hormuz, and Trump renewing a nuclear-site threat ' while a new sanctions action against a Turkish bank pulled a NATO ally into the economic campaign. The common thread: Washington is pressing economic and military escalation against Iran even as it pursues an opening on Ukraine, leaving alliance relationships and regional fronts under mounting strain.
